fact: tests/agents/test-no-general-purpose.sh pins every roleType("...") mention per file in tests/agents/role-type-manifest.txt and maps each Task({ block's description to its expected role (EXPECT).
recommendation: When intentionally adding/removing/changing roleType mentions run `bash tests/agents/test-no-general-purpose.sh --write-manifest` and review the diff; add an EXPECT entry for any new Task({ block.

fact: Regex classes can define 'done' for commands, flags and version strings, but not for prose claims: each review round found another phrasing (#62 plan review escalated 3 times).
recommendation: For prose, run one broad search (e.g. git grep -niE 'priming|knowledge base'), read every hit by hand and record a verdict table; keep the prose regex as a regression guard of known phrases only.

fact: A repo-wide wording guard's negative self-test must include one fixture line per forbidden pattern. In #67 reviewers twice found a newly forbidden phrase with no fixture, so removing it from the list would not have failed any test.
recommendation: Whenever you add a pattern to a guard, add a matching bad line and a `bad.md:N:` assertion. Then mutation-check it: delete the pattern on a scratch copy and confirm the self-test fails.

fact: Hook output runs at every session start and compaction, so it must stay small even on big stores. One streaming `jq -R -n` reduce over the files counts every fact but keeps only the rules that fit named caps; on a 20k-fact (7 MB) store it ran in 0.44 s and added about 2 KB.
recommendation: Measure size with utf8bytelength, truncate by codepoint (never with bash ${v:0:n}), strip [[:cntrl:]] from every emitted field, pass the caps in with --argjson, and fall back to a pointer line if jq is missing or exits non-zero.

fact: Backup/restore snippets must report partial results: count only files actually moved; on restore, an identical file at the destination counts as restored (so re-runs are safe), a different file is a conflict that keeps the backup, and never print 'delete the backup' after anything was skipped or failed.
recommendation: Give every move/copy loop a success counter and an rc, compare existing destinations with cmp (or readlink for links), and test the conflict, re-run and failure paths by running the doc's own snippets.

fact: A doc/policy change to a metaswarm skill or guide can be tested end to end: in a clean container with Claude Code, load an exported tree via `claude --plugin-dir` in a fresh project and ask `claude -p` a constrained question that must answer yes/no/unstated with a quoted sentence, once for main and once for the branch.
recommendation: Authenticate with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set to the access token only (never copy the refresh token, so the host login can't be rotated out); restrict tools to Read/Grep/Glob/Skill; also run the test suites there to cover a different awk (mawk) and no zsh.

fact: A grep check that only requires a policy sentence to mention a gate passes contradictory wording ('the Plan Review Gate must never run').
recommendation: Make policy-wording tests match the full required clause (what runs, when, on what artifact), and run them on every copy (guide, skill, both agent twins).

fact: Requiring a criteria table with one PASS/FAIL/N/A row per checklist item stops reviewers skipping single criteria under a "follow this brief exactly" redirect (Architect API-contract check 1/3 -> 3/3).
recommendation: Have reviewer definitions demand a Criteria check table (JSON: a criteria_check array) right after the receipt line.

fact: Agent-definition text changes can be measured before shipping: claude -p --plugin-dir <tree> --setting-sources project spawns the real agent from a given tree, and stream-json logs score planted-defect fixtures (about $0.40 per Opus trial).
recommendation: Use evals/reviewer-rubric (run.sh, score.js, scenarios/) to compare variants on plain and redirect prompts; run by hand, never in CI.
